primary_meaning: Symbol of divine judgment and fiery destruction upon extreme wickedness, especially sexual immorality and homosexual acts (sodomy)
primary_basis: Genesis 18:20–19:29 (destruction narrative and the demand to 'know' the angelic visitors)
Jude 1:7 (example of those who indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural desire/'strange flesh')
2 Peter 2:6–10 (example of condemnation of the ungodly, with Lot distressed by the sensual conduct of the wicked)
traditional Christian usage of 'sodomy' derived from the episode

alternatives.meaning: Symbol of judgment for inhospitality, pride, excess, and failure to aid the poor and needy
basis: Genesis 19 emphasis on the violation of strangers/guests

alternatives.meaning: General emblem of ungodliness, idolatry, or rebellion that prefigures eschatological judgment
Broad warning against any form of societal depravity or covenant unfaithfulness without specifying sexuality

notes: Traditional and confessional Christian interpretation (patristic through modern evangelical and Catholic teaching) overwhelmingly centers the sexual-immorality reading; the inhospitality/social-justice reading is prominent in modern academic and progressive circles but remains secondary to the historic consensus. The cities function primarily as a cautionary type of irreversible divine wrath.
